title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 175 (Passing of resolution by circulation)

content.overview: Section 175 provides that a resolution may be passed by the Board (or a committee) by circulation if the resolution has been circulated in draft, together with the necessary papers, to all the directors (or committee members) at their addresses registered with the company in India, and has been approved by a majority of the directors (or members) who are entitled to vote on the resolution. If not less than one-third of the total number of directors require that any resolution under circulation must be decided at a meeting, the chair must put the resolution to a meeting.
content.glance: Circular resolution: draft + papers to all directors in India; majority of those entitled to vote approve; ≥1/3 may force a meeting; noted in next meeting minutes; s. 179(3) powers and other meeting-only matters cannot go by circulation.
content.study: No resolution shall be deemed to have been duly passed by the Board or by a committee thereof by circulation, unless the resolution has been circulated in draft, together with the necessary papers, if any, to all the directors, or members of the committee, as the case may be, at their addresses registered with the company in India by hand delivery or by post or by courier, or through such electronic means as may be prescribed, and has been approved by a majority of the directors or members, who are entitled to vote on the resolution. If not less than one-third of the total number of directors of the company for the time being require that any resolution under circulation must be decided at a meeting, the chairperson shall put the resolution to be decided at a meeting of the Board. A resolution under this section is noted at a subsequent meeting of the Board or committee and made part of the minutes. Matters that the Act requires to be decided only at a meeting — including powers listed in section 179(3) — cannot be passed by circulation. Current-law framing: confirm draft circulated with papers; majority of entitled directors; check whether one-third demanded a meeting; exclude meeting-only matters.

sections.heading: Circulation
sections.body: Draft resolution with necessary papers sent to all directors (or committee members) at their registered addresses in India by hand, post, courier or prescribed electronic means.

sections.heading: Approval
sections.body: Approved by a majority of the directors or members who are entitled to vote on the resolution.

sections.heading: Force Meeting
sections.body: If not less than one-third of the total number of directors require a meeting, the chair must put the resolution to a Board meeting.

sections.heading: Minutes
sections.body: The circular resolution is noted at a subsequent meeting and entered in the minutes.

sections.heading: Meeting-Only Matters
sections.body: Powers and matters that the Act requires to be decided at a meeting (including s. 179(3)) cannot be passed by circulation.

examples.title: Valid circular resolution
examples.body: A routine administrative resolution is circulated with papers to all directors and approved by a majority of those entitled to vote. It is noted at the next Board meeting. Section 175 is satisfied.

examples.title: s. 179(3) by circulation
examples.body: The Board attempts to approve a s. 179(3) matter (e.g. borrowing beyond limits) solely by circulation. That is not permitted; the matter must be decided at a meeting.

hypotheticals.question: Can one director block a circular resolution by demanding a meeting?
hypotheticals.analysis: A meeting is required only if not less than one-third of the total number of directors require that the resolution under circulation be decided at a meeting. A single director below that threshold cannot force a meeting.

distinctions.title: Resolution by circulation (s. 175) vs board meeting (s. 173)
distinctions.left: Decision without a convened meeting, subject to limits
distinctions.right: Convened meeting with notice, quorum and deliberation

misconceptions.trap: Every Board power can be exercised by circular resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Matters that the Act requires to be decided at a meeting, including s. 179(3) powers, cannot be passed by circulation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 175 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm draft circulated with papers. II. Check majority of entitled directors. III. Note any one-third demand for a meeting. IV. Exclude meeting-only matters. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Circulation facts; approvals; meeting demand if any; nature of the matter; precise relief.
